# Wizard city homepage — Pages facts and operational risk assessment

Case WO-2a6bafff-7f89-47e2-b497-d5dc4519dd84; formal screening revision 1. Development Advisor working draft, not a clearance, completed empirical study, authorization or publication decision.

## Evidence and limits
The coordinator reports read-only GitHub investigation on 2026-11-27: public repository; default branch `main`; `has_pages` false; Pages GET 404; Actions enabled for all; workflow default permissions read; main branch reported unprotected; branch-rules GET returned an empty list; current main commit `d2cc55a3b872142daff8f6f41f746019bdbb7022`. The current workspace reportedly has no `docs/` directory and no tracked `docs/**` or `.github/workflows/**`. The resident selected automatic publishing from `main:/docs` and states they will maintain the site and own the repository. These are reported facts and resident statements, not authenticated identity or authority.

The Pages 404 is ambiguous; do not infer absence, inaccessibility, eligibility or an existing source from it. Despite `has_pages: false`, current Pages status and source remain unconfirmed. No actual public address has been identified. GitHub documentation states that public repositories can use GitHub Free Pages and standard Actions runners are free for public repositories. Account-specific restrictions, effective setup access and billing state remain unverified. GitHub's Pages API documentation says create/update requires repository administrator, maintainer or manage-Pages-settings permission; the current token's reported admin permission does not prove effective endpoint access or authorize a change.

GitHub documentation: [configure a Pages source](https://docs.github.com/en/pages/getting-started-with-github-pages/configuring-a-publishing-source-for-your-github-pages-site); [create a Pages site](https://docs.github.com/en/pages/getting-started-with-github-pages/creating-a-github-pages-site); [Pages limits](https://docs.github.com/en/pages/getting-started-with-github-pages/github-pages-limits); [unpublishing](https://docs.github.com/en/pages/getting-started-with-github-pages/unpublishing-a-github-pages-site); [Pages API](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/pages/pages#get-a-github-pages-site); [what Pages logs](https://docs.github.com/en/pages/getting-started-with-github-pages/what-is-github-pages). These describe host behavior, not this repository's tested setup.

## Proposed operations and risks
The candidate is a static site in `docs`, branch source `main:/docs`, with a top-level `index.html` and default Jekyll behavior unless later evidence justifies otherwise. Future changes to `docs` on `main` automatically publish; the resident selected this behavior. Main is reported unprotected, so accidental or unreviewed changes remain a risk. No branch protection, custom workflow or permission change is proposed.

- **Public exposure:** Review the exact served files and dependencies before publication; exclude secrets and unrelated content. The proposed page has no forms or analytics. This does not prevent the host from logging visitor IP addresses for security, which GitHub documentation says occurs even without visitor login. No legal/organizational privacy-notice assessment is claimed; City Manager should check applicable requirements before publication.
- **Build/release failure:** GitHub documentation says the entry file must be at the source root, missing `docs` fails the build, and the branch-source deployment uses Actions. Review the deployment result after each intended main change and stop on failure. Workflow-run links are documented; no notification settings or alerts were verified. The resident states they will maintain the site; this does not establish authenticated identity or operational service coverage.
- **Capacity and cost:** GitHub documents a 1 GB published-site maximum, soft 100 GB/month bandwidth and 10 builds/hour, a 10-minute deployment timeout and rate limiting. Standard Actions runners are documented as free for public repositories. No usage, account billing, paid add-on, custom runner or cost has been measured. No paid service is proposed; cost remains account-specifically unverified, not assumed zero.
- **Recovery:** GitHub documentation says unpublishing removes the current deployment without removing settings/content and later redeployment can restore it. Availability, effective permissions and recovery have not been tested for this repository. Use only a confirmed method and separately authorized action; preserve the source content and evidence.
- **Address and links:** Project-site address format is generally `owner.github.io/repository`; the actual address is not known. Both intended link destinations are resident-selected, but browser reachability and post-publication behavior have not been tested.

Proposed controls are a minimal reviewed file set, manual review of deployment runs after intended main changes, a stop on failed builds or scope drift, and a documented host recovery procedure before use. Residual risks include public exposure, automatic release from an unprotected branch, host-side IP logging, unverified account restrictions and untested recovery. No build, publication, security, accessibility, performance, compatibility, notification, billing or recovery test was performed. Pages enablement, deployment/publication, security or permission changes and expenditure remain resident-reserved.
